# Evaluation and Discussion {#sec-chapter5}

The framework developed in @sec-chapter4 ranks six production services from five operational indicators held in the organisation's ITSM instance and CMDB. Before the order is interpreted, it has to earn trust. This chapter therefore tests it from several directions: whether it is stable under varying weights and observation years, whether alternative methods reproduce it, whether it adds information over a single-criterion view, and whether it survives the removal of individual services. A final section reads the rankings against the research questions.

## Evaluation Criteria {#sec-evaluationcriteria}

The framework is evaluated against the criteria set out in @sec-evaluationapproach, forming an analytical evaluation in the sense of @hevnerDesignScienceInformation2004 Guideline 3. Five properties are at issue. Ranking stability asks whether the order survives reasonable weight variation and holds across observation periods, assessed throughout with Kendall's tau ($\tau$). Convergent validity asks whether alternative methods reproduce the ordering, and discriminant value whether the ranking adds anything over a single-criterion incident-frequency baseline. Structural rigour requires the remaining order to hold when any service is removed. Practical validity, finally, asks whether the rankings can be read sensibly against the service profiles they describe.

## Ranking Stability {#sec-stability}

Kendall's tau measures the similarity between two rankings and is well established in MCDA evaluation [@shekhovtsovHowStronglyRank2021]. It scales concordant minus discordant pairs to $[-1, 1]$, where $\tau = 1$ is perfect agreement. With only six services the p-value is obtained exactly across all $6! = 720$ orderings. The small sample limits the test's power, but the limitation reflects portfolio size rather than weak agreement, since p-values fall as the sample grows when a real effect is present [@chenRolesChallengesMerits2023]. The p-values in @tbl-kendall are therefore read as effect sizes rather than accept-or-reject decisions. All figures refer to the standard formulation; the absolute-mode variant is examined in @sec-absolutemode.

| Comparison | $\tau$ | $p$ |
|------------------|-----------------:|-----------------:|
| Weight sensitivity 2025 (equal vs adjusted) | 1.000 | 0.003 |
| Weight sensitivity 2024 (equal vs adjusted) | 0.867 | 0.017 |
| Temporal stability equal weights (2025 vs 2024) | 0.600 | 0.136 |
| Temporal stability adjusted weights (2025 vs 2024) | 0.733 | 0.056 |

: Kendall's tau across ranking comparisons, standard TOPSIS {#tbl-kendall tbl-colwidths="[55,15,15]"}

Weight sensitivity in 2025 is perfect ($\tau = 1.000$): both configurations produce the identical order. In 2024 it is strong ($\tau = 0.867$), with a single swap between SVC-04 and SVC-01 at the top once MTTR and patch recency receive more weight. Temporal stability is moderate ($\tau = 0.600$ equal, $0.733$ adjusted). The movement follows real profile change: SVC-06 rose from fifth to third as its incident load, change failure rate and patch position all worsened, and SVC-01 edged ahead of SVC-04 at the top, a pair separated by only 0.004 in the 2024 closeness coefficients. Cross-year stability is reported as descriptive context rather than as a quality criterion in its own right: services evolve between periods, and a faithful ranking should follow such change. In every run, the lowest-priority position is identical, and the same three services occupy the high-priority half in 2025 under both configurations, which addresses RQ3 directly.

## Convergent Validity Across Methods {#sec-convergent}

To test whether the ordering depends on the choice of method, the six services were re-ranked with SAW and VIKOR and compared against standard TOPSIS. SAW used Weitendorf (min-max) normalisation to avoid the division by zero that classic cost normalisation would produce on the dataset's zero values [@thienOvercomingLimitationsRAPS2024]. VIKOR followed the standard S, R and Q procedure with $v = 0.5$. Full figures are in @sec-appendixc.

Agreement ranges from moderate to perfect ($\tau$ from 0.600 to 1.000). In 2025 the three methods agree exactly under equal weights, all placing SVC-01 first, and SVC-03 comes last under every method, configuration and year. The one substantive disagreement concerns the 2024 equal-weight top rank: TOPSIS places SVC-04 first while SAW and VIKOR place SVC-01 first, and the TOPSIS margin between the two is a photo-finish of 0.004 in the closeness coefficient. The split is informative rather than arbitrary. SVC-01's deficiency is concentrated in two structural criteria, the portfolio's worst patch recency (65.83) and worst unsupported-component exposure (4,054 months), so VIKOR's regret term caps on it and SAW's linear utility weights it heavily, while vector-normalised distance lets SVC-04's 410-incident operational load pull it fractionally ahead. Under adjusted weights and throughout 2025, all three methods place SVC-01 first. The broad prioritisation is therefore method-independent, and the residual sensitivity sits exactly where the scores are closest, a distinction revisited in @sec-evaluationlimitations.

## Discriminant Value Against a Single-Criterion Baseline {#sec-discriminant}

A multi-criteria framework only earns its complexity if it says something an obvious single signal would not. Tested against a ranking by incident frequency alone, the orderings diverge ($\tau = 0.467$ in 2025, $0.333$ in 2024; the full comparison is in @sec-appendixc). The divergence concentrates in two services. SVC-01 rises from fourth on incident count to first overall, because its infrastructure-lifecycle debt, carried in 4,210 unsupported component months and a patch recency of 63.18, is invisible to an incident count. SVC-05 falls from third to fifth for the mirror-image reason: its incident volume is offset by full patch recency and no unsupported components. This is the value the multi-criteria design adds, consistent with @albarakManagingTechnicalDebt2022; the divergence in both years is the same mechanism at work.

## Structural Rigour Under Service Removal {#sec-rankreversal}

Structural rigour was examined by removing each service in turn and re-ranking the remainder. Under the standard formulation the order holds in three of six removals (@tbl-rankreversal); in the other three the changes reach the top of the ranking, swapping SVC-01 and SVC-04 or lifting SVC-06 into first place. The lowest-priority service never moves, but the identity of the top-priority service depends on which other services are present. This is the limitation of set-relative distance aggregation identified by @garcia-cascalesRankReversalTOPSIS2012, and in this data it is consequential rather than cosmetic.

| Service removed | Outcome |
|---|---|
| SVC-01 | Order preserved |
| SVC-02 | Order preserved |
| SVC-03 | Order preserved |
| SVC-04 | SVC-06 moves above SVC-01 into rank 1; SVC-05 and SVC-02 exchange |
| SVC-05 | SVC-01 and SVC-04 exchange ranks 1 and 2 |
| SVC-06 | SVC-01 and SVC-04 exchange ranks 1 and 2 |

: Leave-one-out rank changes, standard TOPSIS, 2025 equal weights {#tbl-rankreversal tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

To remove the effect, the absolute-mode correction of @garcia-cascalesRankReversalTOPSIS2012 was implemented. Vector normalisation is replaced by normalisation against fixed criterion bounds, and the ideal solutions are anchored direction-aware to fictitious alternatives at the extremes of each criterion scale, addressing the cost-attribute limitation that @yangIngeniousSolutionRank2020 identify in the original formulation. Under this variant the order is preserved across all six removals in both years (@sec-appendixc), guaranteed rather than incidental: @yangIngeniousSolutionRank2020 prove that variants with set-independent bounds and ideals are ranking stable by construction. The gain carries a cost, since the fixed bounds must be justified from organisational thresholds rather than sample statistics (values in @sec-appendixa). Anchoring the ranking to a fixed frame, however, changes more than its stability properties.

## Behaviour of the Absolute-Mode Variant {#sec-absolutemode}

The absolute-mode variant tracks the standard formulation closely in 2025: agreement with SAW and VIKOR is $\tau = 0.867$ or higher in every configuration, its only deviation placing SVC-06 above SVC-04 at ranks 2 and 3. Its distinctive behaviour appears at the contested 2024 top rank, where it places SVC-01 first under both weight configurations, agreeing exactly with VIKOR under equal weights ($\tau = 1.000$) and siding against the standard formulation's choice of SVC-04.

The mechanism is the reference frame. Classic TOPSIS normalises each criterion by the sample's own magnitude, so SVC-04's 410 incidents dominate the incident axis and pull it fractionally ahead. The absolute variant measures against fixed bounds, on which SVC-01's structural exposure, the worst patch recency and 4,054 unsupported component months, retains its full weight. VIKOR reaches the same conclusion by a different route: its regret term caps on SVC-01's worst-in-portfolio criteria and cannot average them away. The 2024 photo-finish thus separates methods that register concentrated structural exposure at full strength from sample-relative distance aggregation, and the framework reports the margin (0.004) rather than hiding it.

The variant's year-on-year concordance ($\tau = 0.600$ equal, $0.467$ adjusted) follows from the same genuine profile movements and, per @sec-stability, is not read as a deficiency. The absolute frame retains two properties no other method offers here: its rankings survive every leave-one-out removal unchanged, where the standard formulation's top rank flips, and its scores remain comparable across periods, since the other methods rescale against whichever services are in that year's sample.

The practical consequence is a division of labour. The standard formulation, triangulated against SAW and VIKOR, remains the primary signal, and the triangulation earns its place at the top of the 2024 ranking, where VIKOR's non-compensatory regret and the absolute anchoring both flag SVC-01's concentrated structural exposure that distance aggregation alone underweights. The absolute-mode variant additionally contributes rank-reversal immunity and cross-period comparability, certifying that the primary ranking is not an artefact of sample composition.

## Weight-Space Robustness {#sec-montecarlo}

Because two discrete configurations cannot capture the plurality of defensible judgements a weighting encodes [@grecoMethodologicalFrameworkComposite2019], a Monte Carlo procedure sampled 20,000 weight vectors uniformly from the Dirichlet simplex over the five criteria and recomputed the ranking for each. The absolute-mode scorer is used because each sampled weighting is a distinct decision context, and its set-invariant reference frame (@sec-absolutemode) keeps rank-reversal effects out of the weight-space result. This approximates, in tractable form, the stochastic acceptability analysis those authors advocate. The run is reproducible from a fixed seed (50); repeating it with a different seed changed no reported probability by more than 0.007.

@tbl-montecarlo reports the rank-acceptability distribution for 2025. The bottom of the ranking is close to weight-independent: SVC-03 occupies the lowest priority in 98.3% of weightings. The top is a property of the cluster rather than a single service: rank 1 falls to SVC-01, SVC-06 or SVC-04 in every single draw, split 40.7%, 32.3% and 27.0% respectively. The extreme low priority is thus robust to any weighting, while the single top service is weight-dependent within a stable three-service cluster, consistent with @sec-absolutemode, which addresses RQ3.

| Service | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SVC-01 | 0.4073 | 0.2100 | 0.2666 | 0.1162 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| SVC-02 | 0.0000 | 0.0980 | 0.2346 | 0.2974 | 0.3525 | 0.0174 |
| SVC-03 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0175 | 0.9825 |
| SVC-04 | 0.2697 | 0.3468 | 0.1588 | 0.2247 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| SVC-05 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.1180 | 0.2899 | 0.5920 | 0.0000 |
| SVC-06 | 0.3230 | 0.3453 | 0.2220 | 0.0718 | 0.0379 | 0.0000 |

: Rank-acceptability distribution, absolute-mode TOPSIS, 2025 (20,000 weight samples, seed 50); cells are rank probabilities {#tbl-montecarlo tbl-colwidths="[22,13,13,13,13,13,13]"}

Repeating the analysis on 2024 data yields a flatter distribution (@tbl-appc-montecarlo2024): SVC-03 occupies the lowest rank in 75.2% of weightings rather than 98.3%, and the top rank spreads across three services, with SVC-01 taking it in 55.8% of draws, SVC-04 in 30.8% and SVC-02 in 13.4%. This mirrors the weaker 2024 figures in @sec-stability and has the same cause, the more compressed 2024 profiles, confirming that weight sensitivity here is a property of the data rather than of the method.

## Practical Validity {#sec-practicalvalidity}

Three services illustrate what the rankings capture. SVC-01 holds rank 1 under both configurations, pairing a modest incident count (64 per year, fourth of six) with the portfolio's highest MTTR (45.35 hours), a patch recency of 63.18 and 4,210 unsupported component months, by far the largest exposure recorded. The indicators mapped in @tbl-indicators-lit place this debt in the infrastructure lifecycle, vulnerability and infrastructure/platform dimensions [@hakiDigitalNudgingTechnical2023; @nordExamplesTechnicalDebts2021]. This is the signal the framework is built to surface: a service that looks quiet on incident metrics while carrying dominant structural debt that only multi-criteria analysis brings into view. SVC-04 holds rank 2 with the mirror-image profile: the highest incident frequency (574 per year), an MTTR of 41.91 hours and a CFR of 3.38, yet no unsupported components and full patch recency, the indicators of architectural and process debt [@detoledoReducingIncidentsMicroservices2021; @nordExamplesTechnicalDebts2021]. SVC-03 has the lowest priority in every run, with the fewest incidents, low MTTR and CFR, full patch recency and no unsupported components, and is the reference case for a well-maintained service. The one point where the methods disagree, the 2024 contest between SVC-01 and SVC-04 for the top rank, is examined in @sec-absolutemode.

These results address RQ2. A cross-sectional design cannot establish whether the observed metrics are downstream effects of technical debt severity or arise from other operational factors, so proxy validity is assessed on the basis of convergence with theory rather than demonstrated causal mechanism. The rankings match the debt profiles the literature predicts for each position [@hakiDigitalNudgingTechnical2023; @ramasubbuControllingTechnicalDebt2021; @nordExamplesTechnicalDebts2021], yielding an ordinal signal readable against @tbl-indicators-lit.

## Limitations of the Evaluation {#sec-evaluationlimitations}

Every strand of the evaluation draws on the same dataset and indicator set used to build the framework, so the triangulation and baseline comparisons establish convergent and discriminant validity but not criterion validity against an independent measure of technical debt, for which none exists for the non-code debt in scope. External validation is the main avenue for future work. The six-service portfolio also limits the power of the Kendall's tau tests, since $\tau = 0.600$ cannot reach conventional significance across only 720 permutations even where agreement is substantively meaningful. The method disagreement documented in @sec-convergent and @sec-absolutemode adds a further boundary: the framework supports cluster-level confidence, but the single top rank is contested within the SVC-01, SVC-04 and SVC-06 cluster across the weight space, and it turns on whether concentrated structural exposure is judged more urgent than diffuse operational debt, a compensability judgement the framework informs rather than settles. Finally, the cross-sectional design captures a single snapshot, so a service mid-remediation may look worse than warranted and one whose debt is still growing may not yet show its full consequences; longitudinal evaluation is flagged in @sec-chapter6, and the data quality limitations in @sec-datalimitations apply here, with middle-position rankings in particular warranting careful reading.
